value.first: For a 3am waking at 18 months, the fix is graduated check-ins - the Ferber method. It's one of the best-studied approaches there is: across 52 studies, behavioural sleep methods worked in most of them, with over 80 percent of kids clearly improving and holding at 3-6 months. The reason it works on 3am is that a child who can fall asleep alone at bedtime can also fall BACK asleep alone at 3am.
value.second: Pick a clear week - no travel, no illness. Same 20-30 min wind-down nightly: bath, feed, book, bed, feed before the book. Into the crib drowsy but awake, goodnight phrase, leave. Night 1, wait 3 min, then 5, then 10, then 10 each time. Checks are 1-2 min: lights off, same short phrase, brief pat, leave even mid-cry. No pickup, no feed. At 3am, run that same night's sequence from the start.
value.third: Night 2: 5/10/12. Night 3: 10/12/15, then keep stretching to 12/15/17, 15/17/20, 17/20/25, 20/25/30. Expect night 2 or 3 to be worse - that spike is the pattern breaking, not failing. If he's in a bed, not a crib, use the chair method instead. Working looks like shorter settling within the week. If he snores, mouth-breathes or pauses in his breathing at night, see your doctor first. I'll check in Thursday.
